title: Stable blowdown quotient and its factorization through partial exceptional contractions
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $(P,M)$ be a semistable multipointed $k$-curve [def-trf-multipointed-curve, def-trf-multipointed-curve-modification], and let $r:P\to C$ be a morphism to a $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme]. An $r$-exceptional component is an irreducible component $A\simeq\mathbf P^1_k$ [def-sc-p1-standard] with singleton image in $C$ and at most two distinct points in $A\cap(M\cup P_{\mathrm{sing}})$. An elementary $r$-exceptional contraction means the scheme pushout of $P\leftarrow A\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, with semistable pointed quotient and marking transported isomorphically; the map to $C$ factors through that quotient. For later contractions use the induced map to $C$ and the marking and singular points of the current quotient. Suppose a finite sequence of elementary $r$-exceptional contractions, followed by an isomorphism, gives $\pi:(P,M)\to(P^{\mathrm{st}},M^{\mathrm{st}})$ whose target has no exceptional component for its induced map to $C$. Then for every finite sequence $q:(P,M)\to(P',M')$ of elementary $r$-exceptional contractions, also allowing a final isomorphism, there is a unique morphism of pointed $k$-curves $u:(P',M')\to(P^{\mathrm{st}},M^{\mathrm{st}})$ such that $\pi=u\circ q$. In particular the terminal quotient is unique up to unique isomorphism compatible with $\pi$. Connectedness and properness over $k$ are not assumed; the assertion applies component by component, and the existence of $\pi$ as a quotient which is still a curve is part of the hypothesis.
